llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (searches public company/IP info) but includes an embedded third‑party API key and fetch URLs from an untrusted mirror, and its implementation differs from the described data sources — these inconsistencies merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to query company info from 企查查/天眼查/爱企查; the code instead queries a third‑party aggregator (api.tavily.com) and then formats results and prints links to qcc/tianyancha/aiqicha. Using an aggregator is a reasonable implementation choice, but the SKILL.md does not mention Tavily and the code embeds a Tavily API key, which is a mismatch between description and actual implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the user to run npm install and execute ./qichacha.js with a company name — the runtime instructions match the code's invocation. The code sends the company name to api.tavily.com and extracts text matches; it does not attempt to read unrelated files or local credentials. However, it transmits user queries to an external service (Tavily) which is not named in the README; that external network transmission should be considered part of the skill's scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec, but SKILL.md tells users to run npm install in the skill folder. The package-lock.json shows dependency tarballs resolved from http://mirrors.tencentyun.com (HTTP, not HTTPS). Fetching packages over unencrypted HTTP is insecure and increases supply‑chain risk. Dependencies are common (node-fetch) and not excessive, but the mirror/URL pattern is a concern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, yet the code contains a hardcoded credential: TAVILY_API_KEY = 'tvly-dev-41vi1F-...'. Embedding an API key in source is a red flag: it exposes a credential to anyone with the skill, may incur usage/billing, and means user queries (company names) are sent to a third party with that key. No justification is provided for embedding the key rather than using a user-provided credential or environment variable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated persistence (always:false) and does not modify other skills or system-wide configs. It only performs network calls at runtime and prints results; no additional privileges are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing/running this skill: (1) be aware that queries are sent to api.tavily.com using a hardcoded API key in the shipped code — your search terms will be transmitted to that third party; (2) consider the privacy implications and review Tavily's terms/privacy or replace the embedded key with your own credential or an explicit opt-in; (3) npm install will fetch packages — package-lock lists tarballs from mirrors.tencentyun.com over HTTP (insecure). Run npm install in an isolated environment or update package sources to the official registry (HTTPS), inspect dependencies, and consider auditing the package-lock. If you need the skill only to show links to qcc/tianyancha/aiqicha, prefer a version that does not call external aggregators or that requires the user to provide an API key. If unsure, do not run on sensitive data and ask the author to remove the hardcoded key and to clarify the data source in SKILL.md.
